say: Tidy tables, working formulas and honest charts.
This is the video for module 2 of Data Literacy.
Most spreadsheet problems start with layout, not formulas. If the table is arranged well, every calculation takes seconds.

say: Each sale gets its own row. And each fact gets its own column. Do not write 3 bags rice in one cell. Split it into Quantity 3 and Item Rice.

panel.heading: The tidy data rules
items: One row for each sale, payment or order
One column for each fact: date, item, qty
One header row at the top
No merged cells, blank rows or mid totals
Same spelling and date style every time
panel.rule: One row per record. One column per variable.

say: Put short, clear headings in row 1, such as Date, Item, Qty, Unit price, Amount and Payment.

say: Every formula starts with an equals sign. For example, Chioma sells foodstuff in Onitsha main market. Garri: 6 buckets at 2,500 naira. Her formula, C4 times D4, gives 15,000.
She copies the formula down the column, and each row adjusts by itself.

panel.heading: Formulas that do the work
items: =C2*D2 multiplies quantity by unit price
=SUM(E2:E31) adds every amount
=AVERAGE and =MEDIAN for a typical sale
=COUNT counts the sales recorded
=MAX and =MIN find biggest and smallest

say: SUM adds a whole range of cells, from top to bottom.

say: AVERAGE, MEDIAN, COUNT, MAX and MIN answer most first questions.
Every time Chioma adds a sale, her totals update. No more adding up the notebook at night, and no arithmetic slips.

say: A month can have hundreds of rows. Nobody sees a pattern by scrolling. SUMIF adds up only the rows that match a condition, such as the word Rice.

card.title: Where does Ada's money come from?

say: Ada lists each item and uses SUMIF beside it. Rice brings in 180,000 naira. That is 180,000 divided by 400,000, times 100, which is 45%.

card.title: Where does Ada's money come from?

say: Her items add up to 400,000, the same as the SUM of every amount, and her shares add to 100%. Always run this check. If it does not match, some rows are spelled differently.
Rice is almost half her sales, so she keeps at least two bags in stock.

card.title: Where does Ada's money come from?

say: COUNTIF counts the rows that match. Ada finds 120 transfers, 70 cash and 30 POS, and checks they add to 220.

cards.d: Counts rows that match. Ada: 120 transfers, 70 cash, 30 POS, which is 220 sales.
Category divided by total, times 100. Transfers are about 54.5% of Ada's payments.
With so many transfers, she shows her account details and checks every alert in her bank app.

say: 120 divided by 220, times 100, is about 54.5%. More than half her customers pay by transfer.

say: Bars compare categories. Lines show change over time. For example, Ruth sells small chops in Port Harcourt. Her six weeks total 356,000 naira, a mean of about 59,333, so she uses a line chart.

panel.heading: Match the chart to the question
items: Which sells most? Bar or column chart
Change over time? Line chart
Share of a whole? Pie, 2 to 5 slices only
Link between two measures? Scatter chart
Exact figures needed? A small table

say: Week 4 to Week 5 grew about 14.8%, then fell about 5.7%. She adds a note that Week 3 had heavy rain. Her title says what it shows: weekly sales trending up, Weeks 1 to 6, in naira.

say: Read every chart from the outside in. Sales 70 could mean 70 bottles or 70,000 naira, so check units. On a bar chart, the value axis should start at zero, otherwise small differences look huge.
Then show your chart to one person. If she cannot state the message in one sentence, improve it.

panel.heading: Five checks when reading any chart
items: What does the title claim?
What do the axes measure?
What are the units?
Does the scale start at zero?
Who made it, from what data?

say: To remember. Keep your table tidy. Let formulas do the work. Summarise by category and always check it adds up. And choose an honest chart with a clear title and units.

panel.heading: Remember
items: One row per record, one column per variable
Formulas start with = and update themselves
SUMIF adds by category; COUNTIF counts
Category totals must match the overall SUM
Bars compare, lines show time, pies stay small
